identification.name: Baltic Birch Plywood
identification.common_form_notes: Standard 4×8 ft sheets, 3–25 mm thickness; laser-cutting grade typically 3–6 mm
identification.notes: Baltic birch plywood is an orthotropic material; properties depend strongly on direction relative to face grain. Young's modulus, tensile strength, and compressive strength values given are approximately along the face grain direction (the structurally dominant direction for flat panels). CTE is a representative in-plane value; through-thickness CTE is substantially higher. Janka hardness approximately 1260 lbf (5.6 kN) for yellow birch; standard hardness scales (HV, HB, Rockwell) are not applicable to plywood. Glue line performance degrades above ~60°C. All properties are moisture-content dependent. Thermal diffusivity derived from k, ρ, Cp.

typical_usage: Laser-cut structural panels, maker/prototype enclosures, jigs and fixtures, model fabrication, and lightweight stiff panels in capstone design projects. Preferred for laser cutting due to consistent ply structure and minimal voids.
